direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt requires pure Node ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, no external dependencies, and furl host replacement parity.
Parallel metadata shows actual parallel use, four subagents, completed evaluation, and a failed 119/158 official result.
Status records parallel protocol success, artifact files from both parent and child module trees, and official failure at 119 of 158 cases.
Evaluation summary confirms the current official Docker evaluator completed and marked the parallel solution failed.
Final response claims a parent-owned pure ESM implementation with sampled success and error parity checks.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport trajectory records the parent turn, file changes, command executions, final response, and child activity surfaced to the cell.
Parent session spawned probe_cli and probe_url, probed many URL cases, wrote its own implementation, ran sampled verification, received child reports, and finalized.
The probe_cli child found the source, spawned a nested CLI probe, implemented a separate /output/test2.mjs and lib/url tree, tested it, and reported a full implementation.
The probe_url child gathered extensive executable behavior for host, scheme, path, query, empty-host, and invalid-host cases and returned a probe summary.
The nested probe_cli/probe_cli child ran CLI parsing probes, returned exact stdout and stderr observations, and did not edit files.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is identical to parallel and requires ESM .mjs output, local modules only, manual CLI parsing, and executable-observed behavior.
Serial metadata shows no parallel use or subagents, completed evaluation, and a failed 104/158 official result.
Status records serial control compliance, one artifact tree with test2.mjs and four library modules, and official failure at 104 of 158 cases.
Evaluation summary confirms the current official Docker evaluator completed and marked the serial solution failed.
Final response reports the serial ESM module layout and sampled parity checks for help, parse errors, and URL rewrite cases.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport trajectory records a single local turn with probing, implementation, verification attempts, final response, and no child activity.
Serial session probed executable behavior, wrote one ESM implementation tree, patched an invalid-host error class, ran sampled checks, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no external dependency, and observable executable parity requirements, including host replacement edge cases.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept final implementation ownership but spawned probe_cli and probe_url; probe_cli also spawned a nested CLI probe and independently wrote a complete implementation.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote lib/argv.mjs, lib/host.mjs, lib/uri_reference.mjs, lib/errors.mjs, lib/furlish.mjs, and /output/test2.mjs while a child had already written /output/test2.mjs and a lib/url tree.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final artifact contained /output/test2.mjs plus both parent root-level libraries and child lib/cli and lib/url libraries, leaving duplicated implementation paths in the delivered tree.
parallel.verification: Parent ran representative Node versus executable checks and reported success after normalizing program names and PyInstaller process IDs.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 39 of 158 cases, and the parallel process never reconciled the completed child implementation with the parent entry point.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same task requirements and executable probing constraint, including ESM module structure, manual argparse-like parsing, and furl-style host updates.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent retained all research, implementation, verification, and final delivery ownership without delegation or shared-workspace coordination.
serial.implementation: Wrote one entry file plus lib/path-utils.mjs, lib/cli.mjs, lib/urlish.mjs, and lib/app.mjs, then patched invalid-host error naming.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a single coherent local module tree with /output/test2.mjs importing lib/app.mjs and no competing child artifact tree.
serial.verification: Ran direct sampled commands and a later parity sweep, although one automated sweep was rejected and then interrupted after emitting OK.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation failed 54 of 158 cases, so the sampled checks did not cover enough hidden edge cases despite a coherent single-agent tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual argv, output-path, and executable-observed furl parity requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements from the identical prompt and used the executable to map CLI and URL behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No major requirement-recognition gap separates the runs; the main difference is that parallel distributed probing and implementation while serial kept one local path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent spawned probe_cli and probe_url while continuing local probing, and one probe child spawned a nested CLI probe and wrote its own implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed probing, implementation, testing, and final response as one agent with multi-agent disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping owners and a child that moved from probing into implementation, whereas serial had no ownership boundary to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Probe_url returned behavioral findings early, and probe_cli later returned a full implementation result, but the parent did not establish a shared deliverable contract for child writes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried all discovered CLI and URL facts in one context and wrote one module interface set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel transferred useful findings but also allowed an implementation result and workspace side effects to arrive without a clear parent integration decision; serial had no handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent implemented a custom URL reference parser and host normalizer while the probe_cli child had already implemented another URL stack under lib/url and lib/cli.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented one custom parser stack split across cli, urlish, app, and path-utils modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced two overlapping implementations; serial produced one coherent implementation, although both remained incomplete against hidden cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received probe_url and probe_cli results, but the later probe_cli implementation result arrived before final response and was not reconciled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its own local verification and final response flowed directly from its implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete completed result available at a decision point and then closed without using it; serial avoided that lifecycle risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child and parent both wrote /output/test2.mjs, and final artifact validation retained both the parent module tree and the child lib/url and lib/cli tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation lists one entry file and one library tree produced by the single agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered a mixed shared workspace with overlapping implementation provenance, while serial delivered one integrated tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran representative direct checks and two scripted comparison sweeps that reported all sampled success and normalized error cases matched.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sampled direct checks and a parity sweep attempt; one shell script was rejected and another reported OK after safe quoting and interruption handling.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used sampled verification that missed official cases; parallel sampled more broadly and scored higher, but neither reached evaluator-complete parity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 634.787 agent seconds, 128 LLM requests, and four subagents before finalizing successfully from a process standpoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 392.752 agent seconds, 33 LLM requests, and no subagents before finalizing successfully from a process standpoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent far more budget on concurrent probing and duplicate implementation work but did not time out; serial was cheaper but lower-scoring officially.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed status evaluations failed. Parallel passed more cases, plausibly because it gathered broader URL and CLI behavior evidence through concurrent probes, but its shared-workspace coordination still produced unreconciled child work and overlapping deliverable writes. Serial avoided coordination defects but covered fewer official cases with its single implementation.
parallel_contributors: Concurrent executable probes gathered more edge-case behavior than the serial run.
The parent wrote and verified a separate implementation after child implementation work had already occurred.
A completed child implementation result was available before final response but was not reconciled.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one coherent implementation tree without child handoff or overwrite risk.
Serial sampled fewer behavior combinations and official evaluation passed fewer cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both solutions were incomplete against hidden official tests despite sampled parity checks.
Serial encountered verification-script handling issues but still completed a final artifact.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels are supported parallel adverse process patterns, not exclusive score causes
